text:
Kevin Fiala's season started on Nov. 12, nine months after he was carried off the ice at the Olympics with leg fractures that ended his 2025-26 season. He played 16:36 against the Islanders that night and picked up a power-play assist, and he has three games under his belt now.

Three games tell us almost nothing about where he is. He has one point and three shots, and EDGE's early skating and shot speed readings sit low, which is what you would expect from a player shaking off a long layoff rather than a verdict.

The player Los Angeles is waiting for is clear enough from before the injury. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 89th-percentile rate last season and breaking the puck out cleanly. Evolving-Hockey noted that his goals trailed his chances, putting him at 1.1 expected wins against -0.1 actual. Our talent range for his scoring rate sits around 2.13 points per 60, right around the league average of 2.1. Watch the ice time and the shot volume as he finds his legs.
